insights.claim: All 37 backend API endpoints including administrative operations (db/reset, deploy-to-cluster) are unauthenticated at the application layer; security relies entirely on network-level controls.
insights.reasoning: The FastAPI application registers only CORSMiddleware with wildcard origins and no authentication middleware. The analyzer confirmed no auth middleware detection. Administrative endpoints like /api/v1/db/reset and /api/v1/deploy-to-cluster perform destructive or privileged operations without any credential check. While OpenShift Routes provide TLS termination, no OAuth proxy or edge authentication is configured in the deployment manifests.

insights.claim: The LLM provider layer is pluggable via LLM_PROVIDER environment variable, supporting OpenAI-compatible endpoints, Vertex AI, and local Ollama, enabling deployment flexibility across cloud and on-premises environments.
insights.reasoning: The backend deployment configures LLM_PROVIDER via ConfigMap, OPENAI_BASE_URL and OPENAI_API_KEY via Secrets, and OLLAMA_HOST as a direct environment variable. The OpenAI client supports configurable base_url, allowing redirection to any OpenAI-compatible inference server. This pattern supports both cloud-hosted and air-gapped deployment scenarios.

insights.claim: The Dockerfile uses python:3.14-slim (Debian-based) rather than a UBI base image, which will fail FIPS validation and check-payload gates required for RHOAI distribution.
insights.reasoning: RHOAI components are expected to use UBI-based images for FIPS compliance and check-payload validation. The python:3.14-slim base image is Debian-based and ships a non-FIPS-validated OpenSSL. This is architecturally significant for the RHOAI distribution pipeline, as images must pass Konflux check-payload gates that verify FIPS-compliant cryptographic libraries.
